questions.text:
Let $f:[1, \infty) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function, If $6 \int_{1}^{x} f(t) d t=3 x f(x)+x^{3}-4$ for all $\mathrm{x} \geq 1$, then the value of $f(2)-f(3)$ is
(1) -4
(2) -3
(3) 4
(4)

steps:
$\quad 6 \int_{1}^{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{t}) \mathrm{dt}=3 \mathrm{x} \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})+\mathrm{x}^{3}-4$
Diff. both side
$6 \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=3 \mathrm{x} \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})+3 \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})+3 \mathrm{x}^{2}$
$3 f(x)=3 x f^{\prime}(x)+3 x^{2}$
$x \frac{d y}{d x}-y=-x^{2}$
$\frac{x \frac{d y}{d x}-9}{x^{2}}=-1$
$\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dx}}\left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}\right)=-1$
$\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}=-\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{C}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=-\mathrm{x}^{2}+\mathrm{Cx}$
at $\mathrm{x}=1, \mathrm{y}=1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{C}=2$
$f(x)=-x^{2}+2 x$
$f(2)-f(3)=3$

$$\frac{4}{2}(2 a+3 d)=6 \Rightarrow 2 a+3 d=3$$

$$\frac{6}{2}(2 a+5 d)=4 \Rightarrow 2 a+5 d=\frac{4}{3}$$
eq. (2) - eq. (1)
$$\begin{array}{l}

$$\begin{array}{l}

A cylindrical tube $A B$ of length $l$, closed at both ends contains an ideal gas of 1 mol having molecular weight $M$. The tube is rotated in a horizontal plane with constant angular velocity $\omega$ about an axis perpendicular to $A B$ and passing through the edge at end A, as shown in the figure. If $P_{A}$ and $P_{B}$ are the pressures at $A$ and $B$ respectively, then (Consider the temperature is same at all points in the tube)
(1) $P_{B}=P_{A} \exp \left(M \omega^{2} l^{2} / 2 R T\right)$
(2) $P_{B}=P_{A}$
(3) $P_{B}=P_{A} \exp \left(M \omega^{2} l^{2} / 3 R T\right)$
(4) $P_{B}=P_{A} \exp \left(M \omega^{2} l^{2} / R T\right)$

steps:
$$\begin{array}{l}
A[(P+d P)-P]=(d m)\left(\omega^{2} x\right) \\
d P=\frac{(d m)}{A} \omega^{2} x \\
d P=\frac{(\rho)(A)(d x) \omega^{2} x}{A} \\
\text { also }[P M=\rho R T] \\
\rho=\frac{P M}{R T} \\
d P=\left(\frac{P M}{R T}\right) \omega^{2} x d x \\
\int_{P_{A}}^{P_{B}} \frac{d P}{P}=\frac{\omega^{2} M}{R T} \int_{0}^{\ell} x d x \\
\ell n\left(\frac{P_{B}}{P_{A}}\right)=\frac{\omega^{2} \ell^{2} M}{2 R T} \\
P_{B}=P_{A} e^{\frac{M \omega^{2} \ell^{2}}{2 R T}}
\end{array}$$
